messages.subject: QC subplot for decoy peptides - Why?
parts:
Hi MSstats team,

I am primarily using MSstats on the R command line, but lately I executed a QC from skyline 3.5 using MStstats as external tool. My document contains 12,209 peptides including decoys (50%). These decoys are visible as a single protein, named decoys in the skyline target tree. When I execute the MStstats analysis the following is displayed in the immediate window of skyline:

Getting the summarization by Tukey's median polish per subplot for protein  Decoys ( 1  of  1365 )

MSstats tries to create a subplot for the Decoys protein containing more than 7000 unrelated decoy peptides. How sensible is that? Especially since skyline knows that these peptides are decoys (they were created using Refine -> Add decoy peptides). In addition, this operation takes foreeeeeever. How can I force MSstats to use only target peptides to create QC plots?

Greetings,
Tobi

messages.author: 085b00b73e467d88
messages.subject: Re: QC subplot for decoy peptides - Why?
parts:
Hi Tobi,

A significant amount of the entries are decoy as you mentioned, which would affect the normalization of real proteins and it may not be sensible to process all of them together. The current version of MSstats does not recognize the decoy entries automatically. So a get-around is to get rid of those decoy entries prior to running MSstats. If you run MSstats in an R environment, it should be straightforward to do that. 

Best,
Tsung-Heng
